sentences.text: The injunction granted by the High Court prevents Ryan Bridge and Raise the Colours from attaching flags and other items to public property Birmingham City Council has won a High Court injunction preventing unauthorised flags being attached to lamp-posts and other highway infrastructure across the city.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: The authority sought the order after thousands of St George's flags and union jacks were put up by supporters of anti-migrant group Raise the Colours from summer 2025 onwards.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: Council lawyers argued the displays created safety risks and fuelled tensions, while campaigners said the move would restrict freedom of expression.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: Judge Emma Kelly said there was a "compelling need" to grant the interim injunction.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: In her ruling, the judge said it would last until trial or further order of the court.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: The order applies to Raise the Colours' leader Ryan Bridge; Ben Cullen, who is also associated with the group; and persons unknown from attaching flags to street furniture and highway infrastructure.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: It also grants a power of arrest against Bridge and persons unknown, meaning police could arrest someone without a warrant if they are suspected of breaching the injunction.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: The council said anyone who breaches the order could be jailed for up to two years, fined or have their assets seized for contempt of court.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: The local authority sought the injunction after thousands of St George's flags and union flags were attached to lamp-posts and bridges in Birmingham from summer 2025 onwards.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: Lawyers acting for the council argued the displays could pose safety risks, obstruct visibility and contribute to tensions and disorder.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: The application also referred to reported incidents of alleged intimidation, harassment and obstruction connected to flags being put up in the city.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: The court heard that, on one occasion, a man suffered a broken leg when he was struck by a cherry picker being used while flags were being installed.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: The case followed similar legal action in Oxfordshire, where the county council secured a permanent injunction against four named individuals over flags attached to lamp-posts and other highway structures.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: Raise the Colours' leader Ryan Bridge had argued an injunction would breach the European Convention on Human Rights Bridge opposed the injunction, arguing it would interfere with rights to freedom of expression and protest under the European Convention on Human Rights.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: His barrister, Liam Wells, told the court the campaign amounted to political expression protected by the convention and argued the injunction would have a "chilling effect" on those rights.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: In her ruling, Kelly stressed the order was not a ban on displaying flags.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: "The interim injunction needs to be understood for what it is," she said.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: "It is not the court nor the claimant 'banning the union jack' or the display of Pride flags or anything of the like.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: The council said anyone who breaches the injunction could be jailed for up to two years, fined or have their assets seized for contempt of court The injunction covers all unauthorised flags attached to street furniture, regardless of the type of flag involved.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: Birmingham City Council's cabinet member for equalities, communities and social justice, Jane Baston, welcomed the ruling and described it as an "important step" in tackling unauthorised attachments to public highways.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: She said residents remained free to display flags on their own property and said the council's approach had been "proportionate and evidence-led".
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: Councillor Jane Baston called the interim injunction an "important step" for the authority Councillor Robert Alden, leader of Birmingham local Conservatives, criticised the authority's decision to pursue the injunction, saying it should focus on resolving the city's bin strike and improving basic services.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: Campaign group Brummies United Against Racism & Hate Crime welcomed the ruling, describing it as "a welcome decision and long overdue".
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: Britain's Worst Bathing Site Inside the bathing site designated the worst in the UK The BBC has been investigating whether discharges of treated sewage might be responsible for poor water quality at a bathing site in Taunton.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: This summer French Weir Park failed its tests on 13 of the 19 days it was sampled.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: The BBC analysed data from all four regulators across the UK for 2026 and found French Weir Park's failure rate of 68% was the highest of all the bathing sites.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: The regulators look for two types of faecal bacteria  – E. coli and intestinal enterococci – that originate either in human or animal guts and can make people ill if ingested.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: So where's it coming from at French Weir Park?
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: The local water company Wessex Water says it could have come from wildlife, agriculture, private septic tanks as well as its sewerage works.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: We decided to take a closer look to see if we could work out where the truth lies.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: Despite the high levels of faecal bacteria and the health warnings, Jenny, Jo and Jo have kept swimming at the bathing site in Taunton Our wastewater treatment system is built on the assumption that faecal bacteria  - from our poo - once discharged into nature will be rapidly diluted and perish.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: The bacteria are known to have little impact on wildlife but they can make humans sick if ingested – so the rise in popularity of wild-swimming and testing of bathing sites have increased awareness.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: As part of a BBC investigation we analysed the water sampling results from this summer across all the UK's 700 official bathing sites on the coast, in lakes and rivers.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: We found that more than 10% of the UK's coastal sites and 37% of its inland sites failed to meet regulators' minimum standards across the summer.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: That difference is likely to be because the sea acts as a more effective dispersant and can dilute and kill faecal bacteria quicker than a lake or river.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: Of the 11 worst bathing sites in England in 2026, seven were on inland rivers or lakes.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: Last year the official advice was not to swim at 12 of the 14 inland river bathing sites in England .
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: Poor water quality has historically been linked to raw sewage spills.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: These are much more likely after it has rained.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: So why, in a summer that was extremely dry, did bacteria levels remain high in so many rivers?
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: In Taunton the official testing data suggests there has been a constant flow of bacteria entering the river.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: So the BBC carried out its own sampling near three wastewater treatment works upstream of the Taunton site.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: We found the treated liquid coming out of the nearest sewage works at Bradford-on-Tone had about 240,000 colony forming units (CFU) of E. coli per 100ml - that's a level about 250 times higher than that considered safe for swimming.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: "The counts from just outside the treatment works in my experience were high for treated effluent", Dr Rob Morley from Index Microbiology told us at his laboratory near Bristol as he peered down at small dots of E. coli bacteria on a transparent plastic plate.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: What was of particular interest to Morley were the results of the test on water samples we'd taken above and below the point where the treated wastewater enters the River Tone.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: It showed 199 CFU of E. coli above, which is fine for swimming and 7,701 CFU just below, more than eight times the regulators limit.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: "You can see where it's seeding the river with pollution," Morley says.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: "If we were to look further down the river, we would expect the levels to get lower with the dilution effect.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: But that does quite clearly show the impact that treated effluent can have on the river." We shared our findings with Dr Andrew Thompson, a fellow at the Institute of Chemical Engineers.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: He was involved in a 2024 report that warned high concentrations of bacteria and viruses were common , external , particularly in the summer when river levels are lower and could cause serious diseases if ingested.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: Thompson told the BBC the levels of E. coli we found in the River Tone were not illegal, or even particularly unusual, because there are currently no laws or regulations about how much bacteria water companies are allowed to discharge in what the industry calls treated effluent.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: Dr Rob Morley of Index Microbiology assisted in analysing the water samples around the wastewater treatment works We also wanted to know whether analysing the E. coli samples from the bathing site could give us clues to where it came from.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: With assistance from researchers at the University of Bristol, Morley arranged for e-DNA analysis to be carried out  to identify whether the E. coli bacteria were more likely to be from a human or animal gut.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: The answer, as is often the case with water quality, is complex.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: There were lots of different types of E.coli in the samples.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: "Some were from humans, some were from animals and some were just generic from the environment," Morley says.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: "It definitely suggests that some of the E. coli is definitely coming from human origins, therefore potentially from that treatment works." As with all of our testing, more needs to be done to reach firm conclusions.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: Both the EA and Wessex Water are investigating what's causing the water quality in Taunton to be so poor.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: But sources at the EA told the BBC that constant flows of treated effluent is high up the list of likely culprits.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: In response to our testing Wessex Water told the BBC its treatment works at Bradford on Tone was working normally and was meeting all its permit conditions set by the EA.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: So could steady flows of treated effluent loaded with bacteria be behind many of the problems at bathing sites across the UK?
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?

sentences.text: "All the sewage treatment works in the UK and in England have permits to protect the ecology and the wildlife within the river," says Jim Flory, a regional manager for the EA in the south-west.

sentences.text: Chief Constable Jeremy Vaughan told MPs he would "excommunicate" racists and misogynists from South Wales Police The chief of Wales' largest police force says he is working to root out racists and misogynists from his organisation as part of efforts to improve trust in officers.
sentences.article_title: Wales police chief says racists and misogynists working inside force

sentences.text: Chief Constable Jeremy Vaughan had responded to a question from MPs about how he and other police chiefs were clamping down on staff misconduct "in a post-Sarah Everard era".
sentences.article_title: Wales police chief says racists and misogynists working inside force

sentences.text: The South Wales Police chief said: "Do I think I've got racists, misogynists, working for me?
sentences.article_title: Wales police chief says racists and misogynists working inside force

sentences.text: Do I think my work is to find them and excommunicate them from policing?
sentences.article_title: Wales police chief says racists and misogynists working inside force

sentences.text: Absolutely yes." He appeared in front of the Welsh Affairs Committee on Wednesday, along with Wales' three other police bosses, as part of its inquiry into the future of policing.
sentences.article_title: Wales police chief says racists and misogynists working inside force

sentences.text: One of the issues being examined by the committee, made up of Welsh MPs from the UK Parliament, is a UK government proposal to reduce the number of police forces in England and Wales .
sentences.article_title: Wales police chief says racists and misogynists working inside force

sentences.text: Committee chairperson, Newport West and Islwyn MP Ruth Jones, had asked the chief constables of all four forces how they were evaluating their forces' performance when it came to addressing misconduct.
sentences.article_title: Wales police chief says racists and misogynists working inside force

sentences.text: Jones noted in her question that "we're still in a post-Sarah Everard era", referencing the 33-year-old woman who was abducted, raped and murdered by serving Met police officer Wayne Couzens in London in 2021 , and that "there have been issues across Wales".
sentences.article_title: Wales police chief says racists and misogynists working inside force

sentences.text: Vaughan said that 126 people had been dismissed from the force under his watch since he started his role six years ago, and that he believed it had been "significantly higher" under his predecessor.
sentences.article_title: Wales police chief says racists and misogynists working inside force

sentences.text: Saying he believed improvements to vetting and training meant his organisation was now "more upstanding than by-standing than ever before", he noted that 22 people within it were currently suspended - which he said was a "low proportion of the workforce".
sentences.article_title: Wales police chief says racists and misogynists working inside force

sentences.text: He said that identifying and sacking racists and misogynists from within South Wales Police was a "whole-organisation leadership effort".
sentences.article_title: Wales police chief says racists and misogynists working inside force

sentences.text: North Wales Police Chief Constable Amanda Blakeman said her force had "pursued individuals that should not be in policing" and had been "relentless in all aspects in terms of anti-corruption, information from the public, about how we'll deal with people who don't live up to" her force's standards.
sentences.article_title: Wales police chief says racists and misogynists working inside force

sentences.text: Gwent Police Chief Constable Mark Hobrough admitted his force had previously had a "very different culture" with high-profile senior leaders "who did not represent the values of modern day policing" removed from it.
sentences.article_title: Wales police chief says racists and misogynists working inside force

sentences.text: He said the force currently had 37 active misconduct cases and 14 people suspended.
sentences.article_title: Wales police chief says racists and misogynists working inside force

sentences.text: He said a staff survey indicated high levels of confidence in reporting misconduct and that the force would deal with them.
sentences.article_title: Wales police chief says racists and misogynists working inside force

sentences.text: Elsewhere in the committee the police chiefs were asked for their views on the UK government's policing White Paper published in January.
sentences.article_title: Wales police chief says racists and misogynists working inside force

sentences.text: It proposes significantly reducing the number of forces in England and Wales by merging existing forces into larger ones.
sentences.article_title: Wales police chief says racists and misogynists working inside force

sentences.text: A review will propose the best way to organise the new forces and no final decisions have yet been taken.
sentences.article_title: Wales police chief says racists and misogynists working inside force

sentences.text: Wales currently has four forces, but there has been speculation it could go down to one, as is the case in Northern Ireland and Scotland.
sentences.article_title: Wales police chief says racists and misogynists working inside force

sentences.text: Blakeman told MPs she thought the current structure should remain in place.
sentences.article_title: Wales police chief says racists and misogynists working inside force

sentences.text: "I'm genuinely concerned about the prospect of force mergers because of that difference that we see in north Wales, and I'm concerned about the impact that  those mergers may have in terms of our communities and the service they get," she said.
sentences.article_title: Wales police chief says racists and misogynists working inside force

sentences.text: "Anything that is centralised tends to see service reduced in our rural communities,  of which there is a large scale across north Wales." She said delivering for rural communities would be "significantly at risk" if Wales went down to one force.
sentences.article_title: Wales police chief says racists and misogynists working inside force

sentences.text: "I'm concerned about the vulnerability and isolation that we would see in the furthest part of north Wales that's disconnected from the point of view of road infrastructure, ability to travel, and is more connected to the North West of England," she added.
sentences.article_title: Wales police chief says racists and misogynists working inside force

sentences.text: Vaughan said a restructure of forces could deliver efficiencies but must be properly funded.
sentences.article_title: Wales police chief says racists and misogynists working inside force

sentences.text: He said he broadly agreed with the "direction of travel" set out in the government's proposals.
sentences.article_title: Wales police chief says racists and misogynists working inside force

sentences.text: But added: "It's quite hard to analyse the specifics because I don't know what they are yet." The UK government has been approached for comment.
sentences.article_title: Wales police chief says racists and misogynists working inside force

sentences.article_title: 'Lip King unbothered' when mum collapsed after BBL

sentences.article_title: 'Lip King unbothered' when mum collapsed after BBL

sentences.text: Despite resuscitation attempts, she died in hospital during the early hours of the next day.
sentences.article_title: 'Lip King unbothered' when mum collapsed after BBL

sentences.text: During the inquest, a jury was played a recording of a 999 call made by Parke.
sentences.article_title: 'Lip King unbothered' when mum collapsed after BBL

sentences.text: He could be heard telling the operator that Webb had "literally just had [the procedure] done" and was not breathing correctly.
sentences.article_title: 'Lip King unbothered' when mum collapsed after BBL

sentences.text: Allanah Kingston, a paramedic for South West Ambulance Service who responded to the 999 call, said Webb had been unable to manage her airway.
sentences.article_title: 'Lip King unbothered' when mum collapsed after BBL

sentences.article_title: 'Lip King unbothered' when mum collapsed after BBL

sentences.text: She told the inquest Parke had appeared "unbothered by the situation" and demonstrated a "lack of understanding that the treatment may have caused illness".
sentences.article_title: 'Lip King unbothered' when mum collapsed after BBL

sentences.text: Jordan Parke, known as the 'Lip King', was under investigation by police but died in February Parke, 34, lived in Manchester, where he ran a salon from his home address, and had a large social media following.
sentences.article_title: 'Lip King unbothered' when mum collapsed after BBL

sentences.text: He was under investigation for gross negligence manslaughter but died earlier this year, meaning the criminal case was unable to proceed, Det Insp Adam Stacey, from Gloucestershire Constabulary, told the inquest.
sentences.article_title: 'Lip King unbothered' when mum collapsed after BBL

sentences.text: Stacey said he had "no doubt" in his mind that Parke, who had received no professional medical training, conducted the procedure Webb underwent shortly before her death, given the video evidence available.
sentences.article_title: 'Lip King unbothered' when mum collapsed after BBL

sentences.text: Of Parke's certificates found in Manchester, "none of them showed any degree of reassurance in degree of their formality", he added.
sentences.article_title: 'Lip King unbothered' when mum collapsed after BBL

sentences.text: A number of cosmetic procedures had been carried out previously by Parke, who, in 2023, had been subject to investigation by Dudley environmental health officers.
sentences.article_title: 'Lip King unbothered' when mum collapsed after BBL

sentences.article_title: 'Lip King unbothered' when mum collapsed after BBL

sentences.text: Concerns regarding basic first aid, lack of lifesaving equipment, and the use of anesthesia without prescription had also been raised, and another prohibition notice was issued to Parke in Salford in 2024.
sentences.article_title: 'Lip King unbothered' when mum collapsed after BBL

sentences.text: He was not registered with the General Medical Council or the General Pharmaceutical Council, and the products he used were unlicensed in the UK.

sentences.article_title: 'Lip King unbothered' when mum collapsed after BBL

sentences.article_title: 'Lip King unbothered' when mum collapsed after BBL

sentences.article_title: 'Lip King unbothered' when mum collapsed after BBL

sentences.article_title: 'Lip King unbothered' when mum collapsed after BBL

sentences.article_title: 'Lip King unbothered' when mum collapsed after BBL

sentences.text: Townsend said Webb had seemed "absolutely fine that day" and had kept her updated with pictures and videos throughout the treatment.
sentences.article_title: 'Lip King unbothered' when mum collapsed after BBL

sentences.text: "At 19:31, she sent me photo of the filler that was going to go in her, I was shocked at how much there was," Townsend said.
sentences.article_title: 'Lip King unbothered' when mum collapsed after BBL

sentences.text: "[Parke] said he was giving her 400ml for free, in total 1,400ml.
sentences.article_title: 'Lip King unbothered' when mum collapsed after BBL

sentences.text: She sent messages and said, 'OMG it kills'." Townsend added Webb had sent a video of Parke giving her the treatment.
sentences.article_title: 'Lip King unbothered' when mum collapsed after BBL

sentences.text: During the jury inquest, Dr Stephen Leadbeatter, a Home Office forensic pathologist, said he considered her cause of death to be "embolisation of hyaluronic acid from introduction into buttocks".
sentences.article_title: 'Lip King unbothered' when mum collapsed after BBL

sentences.text: Embolisation is when something is carried in the bloodstream from one part of the body to another.
sentences.article_title: 'Lip King unbothered' when mum collapsed after BBL

sentences.text: Hyaluronic acid was the filler used in the procedure.

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Fiona the hippo under observation after eating hat The Cincinnati Zoo in Ohio says its beloved hippopotamus Fiona is undergoing emergency medical care after swallowing a knit hat that slipped into her enclosure.
sentences.article_title: Fiona the hippo undergoing care after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo

sentences.text: The Zoo said that Fiona had swallowed the hat about nine days ago and was asymptomatic at first, adding that she was "large enough that a small-ish hat should be passing through".
sentences.article_title: Fiona the hippo undergoing care after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo

sentences.text: But a few days later, her appetite started to decrease, and the zoo staff were trying to encourage Fiona to eat to help push the hat through her digestive system.
sentences.article_title: Fiona the hippo undergoing care after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo

sentences.text: Fiona rose to fame when she was born premature at the Cincinnati Zoo and at first struggled to survive.
sentences.article_title: Fiona the hippo undergoing care after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo

sentences.text: Her story inspired an ice cream flavour as well as a character in Cincinnati's ballet.
sentences.article_title: Fiona the hippo undergoing care after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo

sentences.text: Michelle Curley, a spokesperson for the zoo, told US media that the hat got into Fiona's enclosure by accident, after a visitor tossed it in the air and it caught on a ceiling fan that flung it through a small opening.
sentences.article_title: Fiona the hippo undergoing care after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo

sentences.text: "We probably couldn't make [it] happen again if we tried," Curley said.
sentences.article_title: Fiona the hippo undergoing care after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo

sentences.text: Zoo staff have been providing a series of supportive measures like fluids and ultrasounds to help Fiona recover.
sentences.article_title: Fiona the hippo undergoing care after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo

sentences.text: The latest ultrasound showed the hat passing through Fiona's small intestine, the staff said, adding that she is still a bit dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: Fiona the hippo undergoing care after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo

sentences.text: "Surgery isn't an option for full-grown hippos and our best chance for success with Fiona would be if she could pass this on her own," one of the zookeepers said in an update.
sentences.article_title: Fiona the hippo undergoing care after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo

sentences.text: Fiona was born six weeks early to 17-year-old hippo Bibi on 24 January 2017.
sentences.article_title: Fiona the hippo undergoing care after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo

sentences.text: At birth she weighed 13 kg (29 lbs), which the zoo said was about half the previous lowest recorded birth weight for her species.
sentences.article_title: Fiona the hippo undergoing care after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo

sentences.text: The wider plan envisages linking these initiatives to the railway, which transports minerals from Central Africa to Western markets via Angola, rather than east to China as most do currently.
sentences.article_title: Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?

sentences.text: The hope is that formalising the mineral trade and encouraging investment could help curb illicit markets that have helped finance armed groups and fuel instability.

sentences.text: Its importance has grown as demand for copper and cobalt rises, driven partly by the global transition to cleaner energy, as both are critical ingredients for all kinds of electrical components.
sentences.article_title: Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?

sentences.text: The US sees the corridor as a means to diversify mineral supplies and reduce reliance on China, which dominates much of the world's processing capacity.
sentences.article_title: Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?

sentences.text: A US-DR Congo strategic partnership identifies the route from the Congolese town of Sakania to Lobito as a priority for mineral exports, while the economic framework agreed by DR Congo and Rwanda envisages connecting regional infrastructure and trade initiatives to the corridor.

sentences.text: The project has attracted over $750m (£570m), including funding backed by the US International Development Finance Corporation and the Development Bank of Southern Africa to upgrade railway tracks, signalling systems and trains.
sentences.article_title: Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?

sentences.article_title: Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?

sentences.article_title: Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?

sentences.article_title: Grand Theft Auto staff 'caught red-handed' in confidentiality breach, tribunal hears

sentences.article_title: Grand Theft Auto staff 'caught red-handed' in confidentiality breach, tribunal hears

sentences.article_title: Grand Theft Auto staff 'caught red-handed' in confidentiality breach, tribunal hears

sentences.article_title: Grand Theft Auto staff 'caught red-handed' in confidentiality breach, tribunal hears

sentences.text: "The reason why these individuals were dismissed was for that reason – flouting of contractual policies and obligations." Managers were also said to be "vilified" in some posts on the server and the "most vitally protected resource" - Grand Theft Auto 6 - was discussed "liberally".
sentences.article_title: Grand Theft Auto staff 'caught red-handed' in confidentiality breach, tribunal hears

sentences.text: Cordrey added Rockstar was "obsessed by confidentiality".
sentences.article_title: Grand Theft Auto staff 'caught red-handed' in confidentiality breach, tribunal hears

sentences.article_title: Grand Theft Auto staff 'caught red-handed' in confidentiality breach, tribunal hears

sentences.text: He said union membership and activities had nothing to do with the dismissals.
sentences.article_title: Grand Theft Auto staff 'caught red-handed' in confidentiality breach, tribunal hears

sentences.text: In a statement, a spokesperson for Rockstar Games said: "Rockstar Games' position has been clear and consistent throughout.
sentences.article_title: Grand Theft Auto staff 'caught red-handed' in confidentiality breach, tribunal hears

sentences.text: "Individuals across the UK and Canada were dismissed for gross misconduct following the sharing of confidential company information, not because of alleged trade union membership or activity.

sentences.text: "The tribunal has heard our evidence and seen the facts, and the hearing has not yet concluded.
sentences.article_title: Grand Theft Auto staff 'caught red-handed' in confidentiality breach, tribunal hears

sentences.text: Current rules say all new cars must be zero emission by 2035 The UK is likely to miss legally binding climate targets if the government reduces electric vehicle (EV) targets, independent adviser the Climate Change Committee (CCC) has warned.
sentences.article_title: Government risks missing climate targets if EV rules weakened, adviser warns

sentences.text: In a letter to Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander, the CCC argues that weakening the targets would result in "economic and energy security costs" and leave households "more exposed to volatile fossil fuel prices".
sentences.article_title: Government risks missing climate targets if EV rules weakened, adviser warns

sentences.text: The CCC says that switching to an electric vehicle can save a typical household around £800 a year, with fewer people benefiting if the targets were watered down.
sentences.article_title: Government risks missing climate targets if EV rules weakened, adviser warns

sentences.text: The warning comes after weeks of speculation that the government plans to announce changes to the EV targets.
sentences.article_title: Government risks missing climate targets if EV rules weakened, adviser warns

sentences.text: Government sources insist no decision has been made.
sentences.article_title: Government risks missing climate targets if EV rules weakened, adviser warns

sentences.text: Under the current rules, a "zero emission vehicle" (ZEV) mandate requires 80% of new cars sold in the UK to be zero emission by 2030 and all new cars to meet that standard by 2035.
sentences.article_title: Government risks missing climate targets if EV rules weakened, adviser warns

sentences.text: Companies that fail to meet their ZEV mandate face a potential fine of £12,000 per car, although there are exemptions.
sentences.article_title: Government risks missing climate targets if EV rules weakened, adviser warns

sentences.text: Industry groups have long complained the current rules impose too heavy a burden, calling instead for a "sustainable transition".
sentences.article_title: Government risks missing climate targets if EV rules weakened, adviser warns

sentences.text: Latest data from trade body the Society of Motor Manufacturing and Traders (SMMT) shows that EVs, as well as plug-in hybrids, are driving growth in new car sales.

sentences.text: In the year so far, 26.6% of all new car registrations have been fully electric, the SMMT says, which is below the headline target of 33% for 2026.
sentences.article_title: Government risks missing climate targets if EV rules weakened, adviser warns

sentences.text: "The industry cannot subsidise the transition indefinitely, which is why it is unified in seeking change," he said.
sentences.article_title: Government risks missing climate targets if EV rules weakened, adviser warns

sentences.text: The CCC analysis also argued that weakening the targets would lead to a hole in the government's carbon savings that need to be made in order to meet its legally binding climate targets.
sentences.article_title: Government risks missing climate targets if EV rules weakened, adviser warns

sentences.article_title: Government risks missing climate targets if EV rules weakened, adviser warns

sentences.text: Because they use light instead of electricity, photonic chips are faster, use less energy and generate less heat than traditional computer chips.

sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "With optical chips, you are now where electronic chips were maybe 40 [or] 50 years ago." sentences.text: A jet engine will have hundreds of turbine blades Every time you fly, an extraordinary feat of endurance occurs inside the aircraft's engines.

sentences.text: Hidden from view inside the sleek outer nacelle are hundreds of little turbine blades that can shrug off enormous mechanical stresses and temperatures exceeding 1,500C.

sentences.text: During the 1960s, engineers worked out how to take a molten metal alloy, cast it into the shape of a turbine blade, and then cool it very carefully from one end to the other over a matter of hours.

sentences.text: A single crystal or grain of metal alloy forms during this process of gradual, delicate solidification.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Ashim's footage is collected by a local company, which might have hundreds of people filming their work.

sentences.text: Rashdan Technologies collects and processes such human generated data.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: We go wherever the task is," says co-founder and CEO Shahil Baig.

sentences.text: "For a lot of these people, that's meaningful," Baig says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Making sure workers give their consent and are comfortable with the process is important, he says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: And until recently, that data was not available.

sentences.text: Alan Milburn has said the country needs a "complete system reset" to bring down the number of young people not in work or education - known as "Neets".
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: In a major review, published on Tuesday, , external he suggested a raft of proposals to address the problem, which mostly cover England but he says can be adapted in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland too.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Each of his recommendations will need to be accepted by the government and implemented and paid for before they become reality - and that could take some time.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: So how might today's proposals affect you if you are Neet?
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Major report proposes welfare changes, apprenticeships and tax cuts to help 440,000 young people into work At the heart of the recommendations, Milburn says, is a new Youth Opportunity Service.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: He wants this to be implemented locally, with each area drawing up a plan to help their own young people.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: It would bring together employment, careers, health and practical support, with each young person getting a named adviser and a personalised plan.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Milburn wants areas to begin building their Youth Opportunity Service from 2027, with one in place everywhere by the end of 2029.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Within 14 days of entering the service, a young person would then meet with a named adviser.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Within four weeks, they would have their "personalised participation plan", setting out what both the support services and the young person involved would do, and when.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Jobs wise, Milburn wants there to be initiatives like work placements of up to 12 weeks, structured volunteering opportunities, and help to create businesses.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: He also wants those who remain Neet - despite enagaging with support - to be provided with a paid six-month job, funded by the government.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: The government has already committed to a legal guarantee of job support in theory , but the exact workings still need to be worked out.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Alongside more work opportunities, Milburn wants a "major expansion" in further education for 18- to 24 year-olds, as well as more apprenticeship places.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Over the next decade, he wants the number of young people completing an apprenticeship to double, and for apprenticeships to rival university as an option for school leavers.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Colleges should also get new funding for participation and work-readiness, the review says, initially targeted at 16- and 17-year-olds who are Neet or at serious risk of becoming so.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: He also wants the government to develop new industry-led technical colleges and specialist campuses.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: If the reforms are enacted, Milburn says young people should have better access to high-quality further education and apprenticeships by 2028.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Under the proposals, schools, colleges and universities would be judged by whether pupils make successful transitions into further learning and work, rather than just academic achievements.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: By 2036, he wants 35% of each year group to have started a high-quality apprenticeship by age 25.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: The young people caught up in Britain's Neets crisis At a glance: Key proposals from Milburn's Neets report Milburn has said he wants a fundamental transformation of how mental health support for young people is delivered.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Young people who are Neet should be guaranteed fast-track access to services within three months, according to his recommendations.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: This would include things like vocational rehabilitation, talking therapies and counselling as part of a young person's plan with their local Youth Opportunity Service - which would be rolled out between 2027 and 2029 under the plans.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: There has been a big rise in mental distress among children and young people in recent years, and Milburn's report comes at a time the NHS is facing huge pressures.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Milburn wants mental health support to be available for all young people digitally, without needing a diagnosis.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Some areas are already using these approaches, but scaling them up would be a major challenge and would take a long time to introduce across the board.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Plus, Milburn wants "fitness to work" notes to be taken out of the hands of GPs and put into community work and health teams, and for them to be "a trigger for help - not simply a certificate of absence".
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Milburn wants these changes to begin in 2027 and would be linked to the Youth Opportunity Service rollout, which would be complete by 2029 under the plans.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Milburn has said he wants companies to be incentivised to employ more young people, with the report highlighting a competitive jobs market and applicants who often fail to hear back from potential employers.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: The report includes three asks of employers: to create more genuine first jobs, more first-job apprenticeships and much wider access to meaningful work experience.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Plus, Milburn wants large employers to find ways of responding to rejected job applicants.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: These changes should be felt by both employers and the young people looking for jobs by 2029, the report says.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: To achieve this, the report suggests a £3,000 payment for employers who take on someone who has been Neet for six months, with a further premium of £2,000 available if they are a small business.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: An extra payment of £2,000 would go to employers taking on somebody taking substantially greater barriers, such as care leavers or disabled young people.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: These payments are proposed to be part of changes to the Youth Jobs Grant - which already exists , external - but they would expand under Milburn's proposals from 2027.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Sweeping reforms are needed to help 440,000 more young people into work, according to former minister Alan Milburn.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: Almost one million young people aged 16 to 24 in the UK are not in education, employment or training - or "Neet" - a current rate of 13%, which Milburn wants to fall to around 5% within a decade.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: His government-commissioned review, due to be published in full on Tuesday, calls for ministers to intervene from early childhood through to adulthood, funded in part by radical changes to benefits for young adults.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: But Helen Whately, Conservative shadow work and pensions secretary, said Milburn's proposals were in parts "too cautious" and too reliant on the "expensive hand of the state".
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: Many of the review's proposed changes are specific to England, with some welfare and tax measures applying across all home nations.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: Milburn, a former Labour health secretary, says extensive change is needed to avoid a "lost generation", and address what he describes as a "moral" crisis.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: "We've got to get on with it, it's going to take time but I want to make sure every young person has a chance to earn or learn," he told BBC Breakfast on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: The review says that, in 2024/25, for every £1 spent helping young people into work or education, £25 was spent on youth benefits.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: By 2036, it says the aim should be for that ratio to be £2 on benefits for every £1 on work support.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: "If we can get the benefits bill down, that is a good thing, but this is not about saving costs, it's about improving young people's lives," Milburn said.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: The service would put a young person in touch with a named adviser to help to secure them an apprenticeship, college place, supported employment or a job within four months.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: The review's key welfare measures, some of which have already been announced , suggest replacing these benefits for under-25s with a new Youth Allowance at the current base rate of Universal Credit for young people, and a new Additional Cost Allowance to replace Pip.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: The minority of young people who are unable to ever work would be supported through a new Severe and Complex Needs Insurance.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: Kat, 21, from Devon, currently gets Universal Credit with the health top-up, so is potentially at risk of receiving a much lower level of benefits under the proposed new system.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: She has fluctuating physical and mental health problems, including occasional seizures caused by functional neurological disorder, which recently left her needing crutches.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: Kat says her health issues limit her ability to find work Kat says she "really wants to work", but says she has to rely on welfare support as she has been unable to find a job where she can be employed in a "safe way" because of her health.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: Milburn, a Labour MP from 1992 to 2010, says many young people are desperate for opportunity, but that many get knocked back repeatedly.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: Josh, 19, has spent three years looking for work while on Universal Credit with the support of youth employment charity Spear.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: Although they help him with applications to prospective employers, Josh says "none of them are getting back, and if they do they say you've not got the spot".
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: Grace Coates, who manages Spear St Helens, says she wants to see "more openness to employing people with limited experience".
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: Josh has been looking for work for three years Milburn's review will suggest gradually lowering the rate of National Insurance which employers pay for young adult employees to make hiring and keeping them more attractive.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: The existing Youth Jobs Grant, where employers receive £3,000 for hiring a young person who has been looking for work for six months, would be retained under the recommendations.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: So would the existing Jobs Guarantee, in which the government underwrites the cost of a paid six-month job.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: The government has recently announced that young adults will be eligible for the guarantee after 12 months of being on Universal Credit and looking for work, rather than the current 18 months.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: The Institute for Fiscal Studies has said reforms will have a greater chance of success if support for young people is balanced with incentives for businesses to hire them.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: It said that while cutting benefit entitlements would reduce the cash young people receive immediately, it might take longer for an increase in employment to make up for that for some young adults.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: Responding to the Milburn review proposals, the Conservatives' Whately said: "Where Milburn gets it right, we'll back him," but added that the review "fails to bring down the welfare bill, proposes billions more in government spending and won't make the slightest difference for young people stuck on welfare now".
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: Liberal Democrat deputy leader Daisy Cooper said cutting national insurance for young workers would "only partly undo the damage of Labour's job tax".
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: She said her party's plans would "shut off the Neets pipeline at source, with 100 hours of real work experience before 18 and a careers coach for every young person".
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: Reform UK's shadow education secretary Suella Braverman said the 10-year wait to see changes from Milburn's proposals "would be consigning another generation to the scrap heap".

sentences.text: "Reform UK would act now to axe Labour's jobs tax, double the number of apprenticeships and end university scam courses that laden students with debt," she said.

sentences.text: For the Greens, deputy leader Mothin Ali said Milburn's proposals announced so far were "extremely concerning", adding: "There is an alternative to threatening vulnerable people with benefits they need, an alternative to unsuitable short-term work." sentences.text: Too many university students can use AI to complete assessments without staff finding out, the higher education regulator in England has said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The Office for Students (OfS) said "a significant proportion" of assessments are unsupervised and many can be completed to a high standard with AI, sometimes in minutes.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It said this posed a "significant risk" to their credibility, and closed-book and practical exams were the most effective forms of assessments.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities UK said many institutions had "made substantial changes" to make assessments "AI-proof".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities that do not meet OfS quality standards could soon be banned from charging increased tuition fees or have caps imposed on their student numbers, under proposals that are now being consulted on.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The new research from the OfS and Advance HE, a charity that gives awards for teaching excellence, is based on the views of 244 higher education staff and 91 students from at least 127 universities.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It said "a significant proportion of assessments" were in "unsupervised, non-controlled formats where AI can be accessed by students completing them".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "Many of these can be completed to a high standard using AI tools with limited engagement from students," it added.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It also concluded it was "frequently possible" for students to use AI "in ways that cannot be reliably detected".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Unsupervised assessment can include coursework, but also remote online exams.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: They were rolled out widely during Covid, and research from Swansea University , external last year suggests 93 universities in the UK still use them in some form.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Josh Fleming, director of strategy and delivery at the OfS, said there were "fantastic" examples of universities seizing opportunities presented by AI, but there should be "far greater use of AI-free assessment".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "It also presents a generational risk to the system as it stands, threatening to undermine students' learning and institutions' ability to assess them," he said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Kathryn Harrison-Graves, deputy chief executive at Advance HE, said students wanted "greater clarity about what is expected of them" but staff had "varying levels of confidence and support".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Some staff, meanwhile, were receiving lots of assignments that looked the same, and did not think their institution's assessments were "fit for purpose".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Other staff described a "polarised atmosphere" between students who used AI and other "conscientious objectors" who avoided it on environmental and other grounds.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The research said AI literacy for students was important during and after university, and some institutions were clearly communicating to students where AI can and cannot be used in assessments.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: But it said there was "an urgent need" to ensure that remote or "non-secure" assessments "maintain their validity despite the availability of AI tools, meaning they effectively assess the knowledge and skills they are designed to measure".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "If it becomes possible to complete an assessment using AI without the knowledge and skills being tested, the assessment should be replaced," it added.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities UK, which represents more than 140 institutions, said universities were "making significant progress" adapting to AI.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "There is further to go but many have made substantial changes to how they assess students.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: This includes more in-person exams, presentations, vivas, process-based assessment and assessments that integrate AI in a controlled way," a spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "It's time to get rid of the outdated methods, that have been kept around in the name of tradition, and instead encourage the innovative practice we see across the sector, co-designed with students based on what they want from higher education," he said.

sentences.text: A million young people are being offered a free meningitis B vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It comes after concerns over the UK's largest and fastest growing outbreak that happened in Kent earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Nearly 90,000 doses of the vaccine have already been given, with 135,000 more booked in for the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: So who needs the vaccine, what's in it and where can you get it for free?
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine offers protection against a dangerous strain of meningitis called meningitis B (MenB) that caused the outbreak in Kent.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine does not contain any live bacteria and cannot cause meningitis.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It is common to get some swelling, redness or tenderness where you have the injection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You may also get a mild fever, nausea, headache or muscle aches but these symptoms should disappear after one or two days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: More serious side effects are rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bookings can be made at high street pharmacies across England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Seventeen and 18-year-olds can book via the NHS National Booking Service , external if they are already registered with a GP , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Other students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time can also contact a participating pharmacy.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The boys in Mandela have been convicted of serious offences Students intently focus on maths formulas written on a board before lowering their heads and taking notes as the teacher works through a sum.
sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.text: The teacher's voice and the scratch of pens fill the room.
sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.text: At first glance, this could be any classroom in South Korea.
sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.text: But thick metal bars cover the windows and the students are wearing blue prison uniforms and rubber shoes emblazoned with the words "Korea Correctional Service".
sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.text: This is Mandela Boys' School, an education facility for young prisoners inside the Seoul Southern Correctional Institution in Guro, south-west Seoul.
sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.text: In South Korea, young people who are sentenced to imprisonment by a criminal court must serve their time in prison.
sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.text: "The boys here have committed serious offences and received criminal sentences," Jeong Yeo-gyeong, a correctional officer in the Korea Correctional Service's social reintegration division, told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.text: "As well as theft, there is a high proportion of serious offences, including violence, bodily injury, sexual violence and robbery." But by opening educational institutes like Mandela, authorities are hoping to give these young offenders a chance to better their lives after they serve out their sentences.
sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.text: Opened by the justice ministry in March 2023, it allows boys who were aged 17 and under when their sentences became final to prepare for school equivalency exams as well as the Suneung - the country's notoriously difficult university entrance examination - while still serving their sentences.
sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.text: Held every November, the Suneung is an infamous eight-hour marathon of back-to-back exams.
sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.text: Students attempt about 200 questions across various subjects, which include Korean, maths, English, social and natural sciences, among others.
sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.text: The country itself comes to a standstill - construction work halts, planes are grounded and military training gets suspended to facilitate an optimal testing environment.
sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.text: A total of 551,864 people have applied to take this year's Suneung on 19 November.
sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.text: Around 30 prisoners are enrolled in the Suneung preparation class at Mandela Boys' School, and 11 of them have applied to take this year's exam.
sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.text: Several boys are sitting the Suneung exam this year and are taking intensive preparation classes Park Soo-young (not his real name), a 17-year-old inmate, has been at the Mandela Boys' Suneung preparation class for two months and hopes to study social welfare.
sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.text: He tells the BBC that he had dreams of becoming a police officer before committing the crime that landed him behind bars.
sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.text: He says he could not bring himself to look properly at his mother during his trial.
sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.text: When he turned towards her after his sentence was announced, she was crying.
sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.text: "Seeing her like that, I broke down too.
sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.text: I wondered how I was going to live from then on, and how I could look after my mother, who was on her own.
sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.text: I think I kept crying for about a week while I was in the detention centre." Looking back on his offence, he says he feels "very ashamed that I couldn't control that impulse".
sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.text: If he could meet his younger self, he would tell him: "Control that impulse.

sentences.text: If you do, everything will be different." "I'd grab myself by the collar and shake myself as I said it." He hopes the Suneung and university will offer him a chance to start again.

sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.text: And alongside Suneung lessons, he works with the students' to change their habits and behaviour.

sentences.text: He believes that while studying in itself does not necessarily turn inmates away from a life of crime, the experience of having worked hard at something: staying with a concept that makes little sense, revisiting a wrong answer and continuing even when grades do not improve straight away, is valuable in itself.

sentences.text: "Studying properly means pushing yourself to your limits, and that takes considerable stamina and patience," he says.
sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.text: "Whether they chose to do it or not, the experience of persevering, enduring and not giving up easily may help them to some extent when they face the difficulties of life after release." He says the material they encounter while preparing for the Suneung also gives them new things to think about.
sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.text: Korean reading passages cover literature, society, science and philosophy.
sentences.article_title: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

sentences.text: There are difficult moments too.

sentences.text: They don't think about the impact their actions or words could have on others." The boys also have a strong desire for recognition, he says.

sentences.text: They're hungry for it." Park Min-yong teaches science to the boys in Mandela Not everyone agrees with this initiative though.

sentences.text: One criticism is that young people who have not committed crimes also face fierce competition for university places: so there is some anger that the state provides offenders with separate education and opportunities to prepare for this exam.

sentences.text: He acknowledges these criticisms.

sentences.text: "Studying gives them a sense of achievement and time to look seriously at their own lives.

sentences.text: That's why I think it matters.

sentences.text: I think that is the most important part of rehabilitation." Of course, there  is no guarantee.

sentences.text: Park recalls a student who had done well at the school but later returned to prison.

sentences.text: "He was doing well when he left, but in the end he came back.

sentences.text: A single meteor streaks across the starry night sky during the annual Leonid meteor shower The Leonid meteor shower reaches its peak on Tuesday night, giving UK sky gazers their best chance to see it this year.
sentences.article_title: Dazzling Leonid meteor shower to peak on Tuesday night

sentences.text: The celestial spectacle runs until 30 November, but the greatest activity is expected on the night of Tuesday 17 November, into the early hours of Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Dazzling Leonid meteor shower to peak on Tuesday night

sentences.text: There could be the chance to spot up to 10-15 meteors per hour.
sentences.article_title: Dazzling Leonid meteor shower to peak on Tuesday night

sentences.text: The shower is made up of dust particles from the Comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which leaves a trail of debris as it follows its path around the Sun.
sentences.article_title: Dazzling Leonid meteor shower to peak on Tuesday night

sentences.text: These particles enter the Earth's atmosphere at up to 44 miles (71km) per second, meaning these streaks of light are the fastest meteors in the sky.
sentences.article_title: Dazzling Leonid meteor shower to peak on Tuesday night

sentences.text: Experts advise finding a safe, dark location away from sources of light pollution such as street lights.
sentences.article_title: Dazzling Leonid meteor shower to peak on Tuesday night

sentences.text: The meteors will be visible with the naked eye, with no binoculars or telescope required.
sentences.article_title: Dazzling Leonid meteor shower to peak on Tuesday night

sentences.text: However, giving your eyes some time to adapt to the dark, perhaps 20 or 30 minutes, will give you the best chance of spotting them.
sentences.article_title: Dazzling Leonid meteor shower to peak on Tuesday night

sentences.text: A wide open space is the best place to be, giving a full view of the night sky.
sentences.article_title: Dazzling Leonid meteor shower to peak on Tuesday night

sentences.text: Meteors could be visible anywhere but the Leonids' radiant, the point from which they seem to appear, will, as the name suggests, be around the head of the constellation Leo, meaning this is the best part of the sky to focus your gaze.
sentences.article_title: Dazzling Leonid meteor shower to peak on Tuesday night

sentences.text: Leo does not rise until around midnight, so the best time to look is after midnight and in the hours before dawn.
