sentences.text: The legal action against Natural Resources Wales landed in the High Court River campaigners are taking on Wales' environmental regulator in the High Court over what they believe is a "regulatory gap" that risks pollution from poultry farms in two rivers.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: River Action UK has accused Natural Resources Wales (NRW) of not doing enough to assess or address any risk to local rivers and and other water bodies when plans for three farms in Powys were approved last year.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: It follows years of debate over the alleged impact of chicken farming on rivers such as the Wye and Severn - in an area dubbed the UK's "poultry capital" .
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: NRW said it would be inappropriate to comment ahead of the court case, but that it would "participate fully in the legal process".
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: The case is about plans to increase the capacity of three Powys farms by a combined 336,900 chickens, bringing the total to 522,000.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: The three farms are Neuadd Isaf, Rhosddu and Llanshay.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: Two of the farms, Rhosddu and Llanshay, are in the River Severn catchment while Neuadd Isaf is in the River Wye catchment.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: Campaigners said the Severn was showing "signs of strain" with regular algal blooms, brown algae smothering the riverbed.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: The three poultry units in Powys are located within river catchments including the River Wye Campaigners' concerns have centred around the birds' manure becoming a pollutant when it is spread on fields and leaches into rivers.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: Nutrient-rich agricultural run-off can contribute to algal blooms, turning rivers green and smothering wildlife.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: Following a consultation, NRW approved permit variations in November 2025, allowing the three poultry units to expand.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: Rather than keep and spread the manure on site, the farms' operators said they would export it for use or processing elsewhere.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: River Action argued NRW wrongly concluded it had no legal power under the Environmental Permitting Regulations 2016 to assess the potential environmental impacts of this off-site manure management, or to take action to prevent or mitigate pollution arising from it.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: Emma Dearnaley, head of legal at River Action, argues there is a "regulatory gap" in the management of off-site manure Campaigners set up a chicken-themed protest outside the High Court hearing in Llandrindod Wells on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: The organisation insisted NRW could put controls on the farm's permit to reduce or remove the risk of manure causing pollution.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: Campaigners believe the birds' manure will spread on fields and into rivers, causing harm Emma Dearnaley, head of legal at River Action, said NRW "decided that it didn't have the power to look at what would happen when a lot of the manure would go offsite" when the plans were approved last year.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: "That matters because more chickens means more muck, and that needs to go somewhere and someone has to deal with it," she said.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: "So this case is all about making NRW realise that it does have the power to deal with it." An NRW spokesperson said: "As legal proceedings are ongoing, it would be inappropriate to comment on matters that are before the court.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court

sentences.text: We will continue to participate fully in the legal process and await the court's determination." sentences.text: Tees Rivers Trust workers have been tagging eels to track their downstream migration Conservationists have spent summer and autumn searching for critically endangered eels to tag as they begin their downstream migration.
sentences.article_title: Conservationists searching for large river eels

sentences.text: The Tees Rivers Trust have found 12 large eels by fyke netting, a method of catching eels with a cylindrical net, around the River Tees catchment.
sentences.article_title: Conservationists searching for large river eels

sentences.text: The team managed to electronically tag 10 of them and the largest was 60cm (23ins) in length and weighted 435g (0.9lbs).
sentences.article_title: Conservationists searching for large river eels

sentences.text: Project manager Ellie Ward said the eels caught this year were not as large as usual and were "harder to catch".
sentences.article_title: Conservationists searching for large river eels

sentences.text: The team has been searching for "silver" eels which have finished maturing and are preparing to head back out to the Sargasso Sea near Bermuda.
sentences.article_title: Conservationists searching for large river eels

sentences.text: Ward said: "European eels start to migrate downstream during autumn and winter, when river discharges increase.
sentences.article_title: Conservationists searching for large river eels

sentences.text: "We suspect that low flows in summer that have continued into autumn have contributed to low catch rates so far this year." The Eels of Steel project is funded by Natural England and the Tees Rivers Trust has been conducting the research alongside Hull University.
sentences.article_title: Conservationists searching for large river eels

sentences.text: Each eel has a tag which emits a unique ping, which provides information about their movements while migrating.
sentences.article_title: Conservationists searching for large river eels

sentences.text: The project aims to discover if the critically endangered animal is successfully leaving the river and making it through river barriers such as sluices and weirs.
sentences.article_title: Conservationists searching for large river eels

sentences.text: Conservationists say it has been harder than usual to find the eels Since 2008, European eels have been listed as critically endangered by the International Union for Conservation of Nature.
sentences.article_title: Conservationists searching for large river eels

sentences.text: Numbers have declined by between 90-95% since the 1980s due to a range of factors including habitat loss, climate change and overfishing.
sentences.article_title: Conservationists searching for large river eels

sentences.text: Ward said: "It is incredible to think about the journey these eels are embarking on, back to their spawning grounds in the Sargasso Sea.
sentences.article_title: Conservationists searching for large river eels

sentences.text: "No-one has ever witnessed European eels spawning, they are a species that hold so much mystery." The team say they are always open to suggestions for netting locations, particularly lakes and ponds, and ask people to contact them.
sentences.article_title: Conservationists searching for large river eels

sentences.text: This video can not be played 'Can you believe it?': SpaceX catches part of its Starship rocket on return to Earth SpaceX has successfully caught the top part of its huge Starship rocket for the first time, after a flight lasting 22-and-a-half hours.

sentences.text: Teenager's family 'heartbroken' by meningitis death Meningitis B vaccine to be offered to a million young people Meningitis is an infection of the protective membranes that surround the brain and spinal cord.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: It can affect anyone but is most common in babies, young children, teenagers and young adults.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: It can be very serious if not treated quickly.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: The cause of the infection - either certain bacteria or viruses - can be determined by tests.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Bacterial meningitis is rarer but more serious than viral meningitis.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: It can lead to blood poisoning or sepsis, and can affect the brain.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: This acute, severe infection is known as invasive meningitis.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: It means the infection has invaded the blood stream or brain linings.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Meningitis B, or MenB, is behind most cases of more severe meningococcal disease in the UK.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Cases happen every year - in 2024-2025, there were 378 cases of invasive meningococcal disease, according to official data.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Symptoms can develop suddenly and can include: a rash that doesn't fade when pressed with a glass sudden onset of high fever severe and worsening headache extreme sleepiness/difficulty waking Two vaccines protect against the main causes of meningitis and septicaemia.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: The MenACWY vaccine offers protection against four types of bacteria that can cause meningitis - meningococcal groups A, C, W and Y - and is offered to teenagers aged 14 years old.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Anyone who missed out can get it for free until their 25th birthday.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine helps protect against meningococcal group B bacteria and is recommended for babies aged eight weeks, followed by a second dose at 12 weeks and a booster at one year.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: The vaccines do not contain any live bacteria and cannot cause meningitis.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Meningitis can sometimes occur as a complication of some other infections, meaning several other vaccinations can also help protect people.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: A six-in-one vaccine given to young children - also known as the DTaP/IPV/Hib/Hep B vaccine - offers protection against diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, hepatitis B, polio and Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib).
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: A pneumococcal vaccine offers babies protection against serious infections caused by pneumococcal bacteria, including meningitis.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: The MMRV vaccine - which replaced the MMR vaccine in January 2026 - offers infants protection against measles, mumps, rubella and chickenpox.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: The MMR vaccine is free for anyone who missed getting it when they were younger, regardless of their age.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Generally, it takes a couple of weeks to get full protection from a vaccine and some require booster doses.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine was added to the UK NHS childhood immunisation programme for babies born on or after 1 July 2015.

sentences.text: That means teenagers and young adults over the age of 11 have not received this jab.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: However, research suggests the MenB vaccine doesn't necessarily prevent transmission of the infection from person to person, doesn't target all the different B bacteria strains and doesn't provide very long-term protection.

sentences.text: Outages and IT failings are commonplace - but not on this scale.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: In the past week, there has been a massive Microsoft outage , an apparent tech glitch which grounded all US flights for hours , and issues for the National Security Agency (NSA).
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: That's not to mention outages affecting the biggest US banks , as well as a major flaw found in a popular programming language .
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: These are all separate incidents - but the fact they have all come so close to each other has got people wondering if they might be linked.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: There is no evidence to suggest this - but they do tell us a lot about how the modern tech world works, and where the vulnerabilities lie.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: As is often the case, many outages were a result of an update or installation going wrong somewhere in a system.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: A network upgrade at Microsoft caused servers to become overloaded and shut down.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: It was also upgrades to a creaky old network which grounded thousands of planes in the US over the weekend.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: Problems with the NSA's internal communication system and, separately, Apple's iCloud and Apple Pay were also blamed on things going wrong during system updates.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: Disruption to payments in US banks has been put down to a "software bug" from JP Morgan Chase.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: The bank says it is not a cyber-security incident.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: But some recent problems are in fact related to cyber-security vulnerabilities.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: AI was used to discover flaws in Java, the third-most popular programming language in the world.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: And researcher Scott Helme also discovered malicious code in Optimizely, a platform which is used by some of the world's largest companies.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: Hackers were able to steal about $7,000 (£5,300) in cryptocurrency before they were discovered and kicked out.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: Let's address the cyber incidents first - and the role of new AI models.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: "I would be very surprised if all of these cyber-attacks and the attackers behind them were not using AI to accelerate themselves," Helme told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: Since the summer, AI companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI have decided it's too risky to give the general public access to the most advanced models before allowing certain companies and institutions to use them.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: In these cases, security professionals can use the same tech to find flaws themselves and alert others before criminals get to them.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: This happened in the recent Java incident , as well as the PHP one - where there was a scramble to patch the flaws before they could be exploited.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: Then there are the outages.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: These are not new - the world stood still in recent years as CrowdStrike and then Amazon Web Services ground many devices and systems to a halt.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: Part of this may be down to technical debt - a term used when operators go for quick fixes to software instead of solving an underlying problem.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: A build-up of surface-level fixes can eventually end up with more serious problems down the line.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: With AI causing many companies to re-evaluate their cyber-security, they may be issuing more updates to patch flaws they have found.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: Outages are often also a reminder of the physical tech our online world relies on - such as cables, servers and data centres.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: In the US air traffic control incident, for example, the problem came as engineers were replacing outdated copper wires with fibre.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is adamant the recent incidents are not connected or coming from one attacker.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: "We are not under systemic attack," he said.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: "These events, one has nothing to do with the other, they are not inter-related." In cases such as PHP and Java, the "good guys" found the flaws, with the help of AI, before the bad guys - allowing them to get together some fixes before the bugs could be widely exploited.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: At the same time, Anthropic, among other leading AI firms, has warned of the risks its own products pose .
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: Outages in particular have an impact on the physical world as they often cause disruption to healthcare, schools and people's ability to do their jobs.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: Or, in the case over the weekend, planes' ability to fly.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Marco Rubio says recent tech outages are 'completely unrelated' to one another They also shine a light on the world's heavy reliance on a small number of players.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: Not just frontier AI companies, but infrastructure providers such as Microsoft and Amazon, which - along with Google - run a huge chunk of the world's computer servers.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: In the PHP incident, the world was holding its breath as one programmer - working voluntarily - worked to issue patches in a form that was easily applicable.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: And Java, run by another tech giant Oracle, is used by nearly all of the biggest companies on Earth.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: "The Oracle Java vulnerability is a stark reminder of how dependent businesses have become on a relatively small number of critical technologies," said Sheila Pancholi, risk assurance lead at consultancy firm RSM UK.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: "Organisations need to know where their critical technology dependencies sit, act quickly when vulnerabilities emerge, and test that their response has actually worked." Meanwhile Xander Van Raemdonck, security engineer at Aikido Security, said the challenge was "knowing whether you're exposed".
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: "Java is bundled inside a huge amount of business software, so many companies don't have a full list of where it runs," he said.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: The AI tools used to help find security flaws are still so new that they will probably continue to find vulnerabilities which have been lingering in code for decades.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: "AI is accelerating discovery on both sides and speeding up how much software gets shipped," said Martin Reynolds, field CTO at software delivery company Harness.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: "So the volume of what developers need to patch is going up, while the time they have to get the work done it is going down." Tech debt will need to continue to be dealt with - which means more upgrades to systems and more potential for these to cause disruptions.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: Plus there is the constant threat from hackers as they continue to get more sophisticated.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: Attackers only need to find one vulnerability to exploit - whereas defenders have to protect against all potential hacks.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: "Attackers can move quickly and carefree, and experiment without risk of failure so they can naturally often move a fraction faster," Helme said.
sentences.article_title: Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

sentences.text: "We're currently observing that small delay between how fast the attackers can move and how fast the defenders can move." The cat-and-mouse nature of the cyber-security game means it's unlikely to end any time soon - and the impact of AI means the stakes are getting higher.

sentences.article_title: BBC launches programme for children forced from school by bandits and poverty in West Africa

sentences.text: After Rukayya's father was killed, she gave up school to earn money instead "It pains me to see other children studying and going to school while I cannot," she says.

sentences.text: Three Girls: Lessons in Limbo features the stories of Hadiza and Rukayya - you can watch the full film on YouTube , external Some attacks have been carried out by militant Islamist groups, but the majority in this region are by criminal gangs, known in Nigeria as bandits, who steal, kill and kidnap.

sentences.article_title: BBC launches programme for children forced from school by bandits and poverty in West Africa

sentences.article_title: BBC launches programme for children forced from school by bandits and poverty in West Africa

sentences.text: In addition, many children in the traditional Almajiri system, which provides Islamic education, are not taught subjects such as maths and science, and are considered by Unicef to be out of school.

sentences.article_title: BBC launches programme for children forced from school by bandits and poverty in West Africa

sentences.text: Canadian authorities say organised vehicle theft is a serious crime threatening the security of communities Canadian police have arrested 12 suspects, including eight Nigerians, in an investigation into an alleged car theft syndicate.
sentences.article_title: Nigerians among 12 suspects arrested in $4.5m Canada luxury car theft syndicate

sentences.text: They are accused of stealing luxury vehicles and shipping them to West Africa.
sentences.article_title: Nigerians among 12 suspects arrested in $4.5m Canada luxury car theft syndicate

sentences.text: Police in the Peel region of Ontario said they had recovered 96 high-value vehicles concealed in shipping containers.
sentences.article_title: Nigerians among 12 suspects arrested in $4.5m Canada luxury car theft syndicate

sentences.text: The vehicles, valued at $4.5m (£3.4m) were destined for export via Canadian ports.
sentences.article_title: Nigerians among 12 suspects arrested in $4.5m Canada luxury car theft syndicate

sentences.text: The trafficking of vehicles from North America and Europe to African countries has been a long-standing concern for law enforcement agencies.
sentences.article_title: Nigerians among 12 suspects arrested in $4.5m Canada luxury car theft syndicate

sentences.text: The suspects face 231 charges, with arrest warrants issued for others.
sentences.article_title: Nigerians among 12 suspects arrested in $4.5m Canada luxury car theft syndicate

sentences.text: Police say some of the accused may face deportation after their criminal proceedings are concluded.
sentences.article_title: Nigerians among 12 suspects arrested in $4.5m Canada luxury car theft syndicate

sentences.text: The arrests followed months of what police described as an "extensive auto theft investigation".
sentences.article_title: Nigerians among 12 suspects arrested in $4.5m Canada luxury car theft syndicate

sentences.text: The investigations began in March in partnership with Canada's border agency after police identified a warehouse allegedly being used to store stolen vehicles.
sentences.article_title: Nigerians among 12 suspects arrested in $4.5m Canada luxury car theft syndicate

sentences.text: Investigators believe the network was led by five people who coordinated the theft, transportation and export of the stolen vehicles, with the others playing supporting roles.
sentences.article_title: Nigerians among 12 suspects arrested in $4.5m Canada luxury car theft syndicate

sentences.text: "Together, investigators linked the network to loading sites, container movements and the transportation of stolen re-VINed vehicles," the police said in a statement.
sentences.article_title: Nigerians among 12 suspects arrested in $4.5m Canada luxury car theft syndicate

sentences.text: Re-VINing is the illegal practice of altering the Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) to conceal its identity and make it harder to trace.
sentences.article_title: Nigerians among 12 suspects arrested in $4.5m Canada luxury car theft syndicate

sentences.text: Canadian authorities have described organised vehicle theft as a growing threat, saying it was linked to wider criminal networks.
sentences.article_title: Nigerians among 12 suspects arrested in $4.5m Canada luxury car theft syndicate

sentences.text: "Organised auto theft is a predatory business model run by transnational syndicates that terrorise families and fund broader criminal enterprises," Peel Regional Police Deputy Chief Nick Milinovich said.
sentences.article_title: Nigerians among 12 suspects arrested in $4.5m Canada luxury car theft syndicate

sentences.text: The move comes amid persistent security crises across Nigeria, including banditry, mass kidnappings and communal violence Nigeria has moved a step closer to introducing state police system after all 36 states approved a motion to create and operate their own police force alongside federal police.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria approves law allowing states to run their own police

sentences.text: The resolution, which seeks to amend the constitution, now requires President Bola Tinubu's assent to become law.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria approves law allowing states to run their own police

sentences.text: It also requires further federal and state legislation for state police to become operational.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria approves law allowing states to run their own police

sentences.text: The move comes amid persistent security crises across Nigeria, including banditry, mass kidnappings and communal violence, which the federal security forces have struggled to contain.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria approves law allowing states to run their own police

sentences.text: But critics fear that governors could use the forces to intimidate political opponents, suppress dissent or influence elections.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria approves law allowing states to run their own police

sentences.text: There are also concerns about the shortage of police officers, who rights groups say are often poorly equipped, inadequately trained and vulnerable to corruption in a country of more than 200 million people.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria approves law allowing states to run their own police

sentences.text: Nigeria currently has a centralised police system, with the federal government controlling the police under 1999 Constitution.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria approves law allowing states to run their own police

sentences.text: Supporters of the state police argue that decentralizing law enforcement would allow authorities to respond quickly to security threats and better understand local conditions.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria approves law allowing states to run their own police

sentences.text: On Tuesday, the Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, said his office had completed the verification of resolutions submitted by state legislatures in support of the constitutional amendment.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria approves law allowing states to run their own police

sentences.text: He described the unanimous backing as 100% approval, exceeding the legal requirement of at least 24 states.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria approves law allowing states to run their own police

sentences.text: Under the proposed two-tier system, the federal police would retain responsibility for enforcing federal laws and protecting national institutions, as well as tackling threats such as terrorism, cybercrime and border security.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria approves law allowing states to run their own police

sentences.text: State police would be responsible for enforcing state laws, maintaining public safety and preventing and investigating offences within their jurisdictions.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria approves law allowing states to run their own police

sentences.text: The federal police would, however, be allowed to intervene in a state on some occasions including serious breakdown of public order or human rights violations.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria approves law allowing states to run their own police

sentences.text: Such intervention will however require presidential authorisation and will be subject to judicial review.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria approves law allowing states to run their own police

sentences.text: The proposed law includes safeguards intended to prevent political interference and abuse of power.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria approves law allowing states to run their own police

sentences.text: Governors would be prohibited from ordering officers to unlawfully arrest or detain individuals or groups.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria approves law allowing states to run their own police

sentences.text: Independent state police commissions would oversee hiring, discipline and accountability.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria approves law allowing states to run their own police

sentences.text: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: Can he finally find a companion?
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: In 2015, a young male gorilla named Jojo took his first tentative steps onto grass.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: Until that moment, the 11-year-old ape had spent almost his entire life in a tiny cage at a private zoo in Gabon, after being taken from the wild as an infant.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: His family had been killed by the poachers who took him.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: More than a decade later, Jojo is settled into a sanctuary – but he still lives alone.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: He hasn't had a family since he was taken, or indeed any gorilla friends.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: Jojo's carers at the Lekedi Foundation in Gabon want to find a companion - possibly another rescued or zoo-bred gorilla – that Jojo could live and bond with.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: But finding him a friend - and bringing them into his life - is not straightforward.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "He's probably the most extreme case of isolation I've ever seen in a great ape," says Prof Gillian Forrester from the University of Sussex, who is studying Jojo as part of research into great ape psychology and how to help rescued animals recover from trauma.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: This video can not be played Jojo's keeper Maxe Anaclet Makaba: 'He definitely feels lonely - you can see it in his eyes' Jojo was less than a year old – an infant clinging to his mother – when he was captured and sold.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: Most gorillas spend the first 14 to 19 years of their life in an embedded family unit but he was kept completely alone and on public display at the private zoo that bought him.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: Maxe Anaclet Makaba, who is head keeper at Lekedi and sees Jojo nearly every day, says it is clear he "craves human interaction".
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "He will even go to the trouble of gathering leaves for us to hold, so that we [trade them] for a treat – to interact with us," he says.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: Jojo also calls out when women he knows well visit his enclosure and then leave, making sounds that silverback males use to summon the females in the wild, explains Éric Willaume, who runs the sanctuary.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "He definitely feels lonely," he says.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: When Jojo first arrived at the sanctuary after spending years in a small iron cage, he didn't look directly at people Jojo is one of the more than 6,000 African primates estimated to have been bought or sold in the global trade of apes and other primates between 2000 and 2023.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: Thousands more are trafficked illegally for use as exotic pets, wild meat, and traditional medicine, the Pan African Sanctuary Alliance says. , external Experts believe when baby great apes are taken from their group at a young age like Jojo, they are left traumatised.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "If they're old enough to understand what happened to them, to understand their family was killed, they just lose the will to live," explains conservationist Tony King, from UK charity the Aspinall Foundation.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "You see it in their eyes – the light goes out.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: I never knew where that expression came from, but I've seen it in gorillas." King – who specialises in rehabilitating rescued great apes – remembers rescuing two infant sister gorillas who were brought to a sanctuary in the Congo Basin.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "They were clinging to each other," he says.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "They stayed together in a little tight ball for about three days before they sort of unravelled.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: When the team rescues a young gorilla from the pet trade, they put it with a group as soon as possible so they can socialise and essentially learn to be a gorilla.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: But Jojo's case is unusual.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: He is fully mature and showing signs of harmful, chronic stress, according to Forrester.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: In a game-changing approach to studying anxiety and trauma in apes, she has used a thermal camera to film Jojo's face.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: This allows her to monitor blood flow, revealing what appears to be a chronically cold nose.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: It's a sign of a malfunctioning stress response.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: When any primate – a human, chimp or gorilla - is stressed, blood flow to the eyes and ears increases.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: It puts them on high alert for danger, but leaves their nose, temporarily, colder.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: For Jojo, this "nasal dip" as it is known, does not seem to recover.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "Being connected to others is incredibly important to our psychology as great apes," Forrester says.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "Having another individual to share his life with would be so healing for him.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: The bonds between gorillas – what we would call friendship - is key to their society, adds Dr Robin Morrison from the University of Zurich, who studies the social lives of mountain gorillas.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: In one recent study, she discovered that female mountain gorillas would seek out females they knew, even if they hadn't seen them for many years, when joining a group.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: And she says a big part of a gorilla's normal social life is "just sitting together quietly sharing space".
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: But Jojo has never been given the opportunity to sit quietly with another gorilla.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: No one knows how Jojo will react to a companion.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: Moving an animal from an accredited zoo would be a decision for an international committee and based on genetics, health and the animals' personalities and compatibility.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: Any introduction to another animal would be done very carefully – perhaps giving them an object that smells of the other before they see each other.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: These slow, cautious ape introductions do happen – when an animal moves from one zoo group to another, for example.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: Forrester has contacted a number of accredited zoos to explore the possibility of doing this for Jojo.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: But those discussions have fizzled out with no sign of progress.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: The problem, she says, is "there aren't clear processes in place to do these kinds of trans-locations".
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: Encounters between two or more separate gorilla groups are complex social events The international rules and processes for moving captive gorillas across international borders - from one zoo or safari park to another - are designed for breeding programmes.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "They're not designed for reintroductions into the wild, or to find companions for animals that might need them," says Forrester.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: And because Jojo, who is probably in his 20s, has reached maturity, King thinks it might be too late for him to bond with other gorillas.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "Jojo's situation is unique, but he is probably best where he is," King says, adding that introducing him to another animal could, somewhat ironically, be a source of more stress for him.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: Prof Forrester studies Jojo as part of research to understand how our understanding of human mental health - particularly stress and trauma - can be applied to our great ape relatives Being alone is also natural, even relatively common, for mature male gorillas.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: According to Morrison, about a third of adult males are solitary.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "When they reach adolescence, they tend to disperse and spend a good chunk of their life on their own." Solo males will try to persuade females to form a group with them, but some don't succeed and may feel lonely as a consequence, Morrison believes.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: "If we think of loneliness in an evolutionary context - this mismatch between the social interactions they want and the social interactions they're getting.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: I suspect feeling lonely is part of the natural, evolutionary drive to attract females." But while those phases – of family life and adult solitude - play a role in wild gorilla society, Jojo was forced into solitary confinement as an infant.
sentences.article_title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

sentences.text: I could finally relax," says Abdulwahab Damdoum, surveying his luxurious new apartment overlooking the Mediterranean Sea, in the eastern Libyan city of Derna.

sentences.text: It is part of a rapid $2bn (£1.5bn) rebuilding of Derna that the powerful Haftar family hope will serve as a model for development throughout Libya, increasing their influence across a country currently split between east and west, with rival governments in charge.
